title: Add velocity reading and writing for vasp format
body:
* Reading: After reading positions, if next line starts with 'c' or 'k' (cartesian) read in velocities similarly to positions (see definition of POSCAR file for MD: https://www.vasp.at/wiki/index.php/POSCAR)
* Writing: If velocities are not None write velocities in POSCAR format. Format string uses .format() convention.
* Added test for the functionality with a round trip of reading and writing velocities
author: SianK

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
The case of None never happens:

```
>>> from ase.build import bulk
>>> atoms = bulk('Si')
>>> atoms.get_velocities()
array([[0., 0., 0.],
       [0., 0., 0.]])
```

I am afraid we will need `atoms.has('momenta')` which checks for the presence of the underlying array (which is *not* named velocities).

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Identifies a bug where the None check never triggers, and suggests using `atoms.has('momenta')` instead.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Could you confirm if we can write it directly without unit conversion?  The ASE time unit is a little bit unusual.

comments.author: SianK
comments.body: I corrected the velocity units. Please check.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Yes (provided that Vasp's format uses Å/fs)

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Questions whether unit conversion is needed before writing velocities, implying a potential correctness issue that may require a code change.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
If it's possible to avoid the seek() then that would be best, since not all streams are seekable (e.g. reading from a pipe).

Do I understand from the comment that we *actually* call this function on an open file handle and then call *another* reader on the still-open filehandle with a different reader?

comments.author: SianK
comments.body:
No, the reading is on the same file which is properly closed afterwards.
We are testing to read another line in the expectation that it might start with 'c' or 'k' (Cartesian), which would indicate that velocities follow (=trial). 
When however reading CHGCAR files the position information is followed by the charge density.
To make sure it is properly read (starting at the beginning), we need to reset the file pointer to the state before our trial.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I looked up in the code that the caller (of which there is only one: ase/calculators/vasp/vasp_auxiliary.py L90) indeed *reads more from the still-open filehandle*.

However the first thing it does is `fd.readline()` to discard a line.

So let's drop the readline() in vasp_auxiliary L95, and then we don't need to go "undo" the reading of the ac_type line anymore.  That lets us get rid of the tell()/seek() allowing the reader to still work on memory streams.

Overall this is quite brittle, but no more so than before.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: After this I have no more comments :sweat_smile:

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests avoiding seek() for broader stream compatibility, and asks a clarifying question that implies a potential design issue to address.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Maybe we should set more than one number, e.g. `vel = np.linspace(-1, 1, 3 * len(graphene_atoms)).reshape(-1, 3)`?

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests improving the test by using more varied velocity values rather than a single number.
